newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian finance minister defends record.
newsitem.headline: Latvian finance minister defends record.

text.p: Latvian Finance Minister Aivar Kreituss on Wednesday defended himself from attacks by his own party, which wants to remove him from his job.
His party, the Democratic Party Saimnieks, is the largest in the Baltic state's six-party coalition.
Its leader wants to sack Kreituss as finance minister as he says he has gone against the party's own political programme.
But Kreituss defended his record and said the International Monetary Fund (IMF) itself has said the ministry has done good work under him.

"If someone says I do not follow the party programme, then I must say I have been fulfilling the government programme," Kreituss told a news conference, where he was presenting the details of the 1997 budget.
Kreituss' dismissal must be approved by parliament and backed by a committee that groups the ruling political parties.
Under Kreituss and Prime Minister Andris Shkele, Latvia's budget deficit has been cut from 90 million lats in 1995 to an expected 40 million lats this year. The 1997 budget is balanced.
These measures were urged by the IMF, which this year extended more funds to Latvia on condition it carried them out.
Shkele has said that if Kreituss is dismissed, then he himself will guide the budget through parliament.
A decision on Kreituss' future is not expected for two weeks, after Shkele and President Guntis Ulmanis return from trips abroad.
